title: feat(spec): signed connector instance auth, with aliyun-acs3-hmac-sha256 signing every request (ADR-0143 D2.3, slice 1 of #26710)
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D6hhjvTokP3gaKQjZx1GtR5)_

domain:server#3 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cxRP1AqTeP2PWAhwGK

Refs #26710

Clause-②: yes (widening: one member added to the instance-auth union; optional members added to the provider context and the materialization; an optional third parameter on `connectorFetchOptions`; two exports added to `@objectstack/spec/integration`. Nothing accepted before is refused)
Metadata-protocol: added

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:连接器实例 `auth` 新增 `signed`(请求签名)类型,第一个签名方案是阿里云 OpenAPI V3 签名(`aliyun-acs3-hmac-sha256`)。元数据只写方案名、公开的 key id 和密钥引用 `credentialRef`;`rest` 和 `openapi` 两个连接器对每一次请求(包括重试)重新签名。
- 为什么改:阿里云、腾讯云、支付宝这类上游不收令牌，而是要求每个请求带上对请求本身的签名，以前在开源版里无法声明(ADR-0143 D2.3)。这是第一片(S1),另外两个方案在后续切片里随各自的签名器和向量加入。
- 拒绝什么：未知或缺失的 scheme、内联密钥(`secret` / `privateKey` / `secretKey` / `accessKeySecret`)、手写 `signature`,以及 `provider: 'mcp'` 上的 `signed`,发布时按名拒绝。数据源借用 `signed` 实例返回 422。不确认会签名的 provider,服务端拒绝启动该实例，绝不发出未签名请求。
- 没变的:`bearer` / `api-key` / `basic` 的请求逐字节不变;入站认证不动;OAuth2 换取令牌不在本片(#26702)。
- 先看:`packages/spec/src/shared/connector-auth.zod.ts`(新形状和拒绝)、`packages/spec/src/integration/connector-fetch-policy.ts`(每次尝试重新签名)、`packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts`(密钥绑定到签名器、确认缺失即拒绝)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation exec vitest run src/request-signing`,看到阿里云官方示例的规范请求、待签字符串和签名逐字节复现，错误密钥得到不同签名。
- 需要你做的：无。契约复审(CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER)待做;Tier S,席位验收后落地。

## What changes

**`@objectstack/spec`**

- `ConnectorInstanceAuthSchema` gains `signed` (ADR-0143 D2.3). It is a union on `scheme` with one `strictObject` per scheme. This slice ships one scheme: `{ type: 'signed', scheme: 'aliyun-acs3-hmac-sha256', keyId, credentialRef }`. `keyId` is the public key identifier. The signing key is only ever a `credentialRef`. `ConnectorSigningSchemeSchema` is the closed scheme list, and a pin keeps it equal to the union's members.
- What the publish door (`DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema`, both authoring doors) refuses:
  - An unknown or missing scheme, at `auth.scheme`. The message names the value it got and the schemes that ship.
  - An inline `secret`, `privateKey`, `secretKey` or `accessKeySecret`, by name, with the `credentialRef` prescription.
  - An authored `signature`.
  - `accessKeyId` is answered with `keyId`.
  - `signed` on `provider: 'mcp'`, at `auth.type`.
- The request-signer seam in `connector-provider.ts`:
  - `ConnectorRequestSigner` has `sign(request)`, which returns the headers to set and optionally a canonical URL, plus an optional `verifyResponse(response)` for schemes that sign their responses (ADR-0143 Q4 condition 2: the seam carries it from the first slice).
  - `ConnectorProviderContext.requestSigner` is set only for a `signed` instance, and `auth` is then `undefined`.
  - `ConnectorMaterialization.requestSignerApplied` is the provider's acknowledgement.
- `connectorFetchOptions(policy, base, signer?)`: with a signer, it wraps `fetchImpl`, so every attempt `resilientFetch` makes is signed fresh. A retry gets a new nonce and date. `resilient-fetch.ts` is not touched.
- `readConnectorResponse(response, signer?)` verifies the raw body before parsing when the scheme verifies responses. With no signer, both functions behave exactly as the code they replace. Neither uses `node:crypto`: signers live on the server.

**`@objectstack/service-automation`**

- A `signed` instance's `credentialRef` resolves through the same chain as the static kinds (#27237). An unresolved reference degrades the instance with the reference named, as before.
- The key is bound to its scheme's signer in `src/request-signing/` (a registry with an exhaustive switch over the scheme enum, so a scheme without a signer does not compile). The provider receives only the signer.
- The service refuses to serve a `signed` instance on a provider whose materialization does not acknowledge the signer. That is a configuration fault naming the instance, the scheme and the provider. Its connection is closed, and it never dispatches unsigned (ADR-0049).
- A key that cannot sign (an empty one) is a configuration fault, and its message never contains the key.
- `aliyun-acs3-hmac-sha256` builds the canonical request:
  - method
  - path, RFC 3986-encoded per segment
  - sorted query
  - `host`, `content-type` and `x-acs-*` headers
  - SHA-256 of the body

  It signs it with HMAC-SHA256 and sets `x-acs-date`, `x-acs-signature-nonce`, `x-acs-content-sha256` and `Authorization`.
- A datasource that borrows a `signed` instance through `external.connector` is refused with `422 VALIDATION_ERROR`, because a driver cannot sign per request.

**`@objectstack/connector-rest`, `@objectstack/connector-openapi`**

- The providers pass `ctx.requestSigner` to the transport and acknowledge it.
- A static credential together with a signer is refused at construction.
- An `openapi` instance's remote spec URL is fetched unsigned, as before. Only API calls are signed.

**Docs:** `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx` gains a "Request signing: `signed`" section and a failure-table row. `packages/spec/docs/SYNC_ARCHITECTURE.md` names the kind. The variant-docs entry and the ADR anchor for the signer registry are registered. The generated references are regenerated with `check:generated --fix`.

## Why

ADR-0143 D2.3 opens per-request signing on declarative instances, with a closed scheme list that grows only with implemented signers and vectors. Q4 ruled A, so the first members are `alipay-v3`, `aliyun-acs3-hmac-sha256` and `tencentcloud-tc3-hmac-sha256`. This slice is Aliyun because Alibaba Cloud publishes a complete worked example, so the seam is proven end to end against a byte-exact vector. `tencentcloud-tc3-hmac-sha256` (S2) and `alipay-v3` with response verification (S3, `Fixes #26710`) each join the enum together with their signer.

## Verification

- **Vectors:** `packages/services/service-automation/src/request-signing/aliyun-acs3-hmac-sha256.test.ts` reproduces Alibaba Cloud's published V3 signature example byte for byte: canonical request, string to sign, signature and `Authorization`. The source is Alibaba Cloud's "V3 request structure and signature" document (help.aliyun.com 2593177), with its own placeholder key id and secret. A wrong key gives a different signature, and the canonical encoding of the query and path is pinned (11 tests).
- **Publish door:** `packages/spec/src/integration/connector-auth-signed.test.ts`. Each refusal is pinned by issue `code` and `path`, and there is a CONTROL accept on `rest` and `openapi`. `connector-auth-grant-kinds.test.ts` still refuses unknown kinds. `bearer`, `api-key` and `basic` parse as before.
- **Per-attempt signing:** `connector-fetch-policy.test.ts`:
  - A 503 then 200 is signed twice with different nonces.
  - A signer header replaces a same-named header, and the signer's URL is the one sent.
  - Non-text bodies are refused.
  - `readConnectorResponse` verifies the raw body, and a verification failure throws.
  - CONTROL: with no signer, the fetch is untouched.
- **Host:** `connector-materialization.test.ts`:
  - The signer is bound to the resolved key, `auth` is undefined, and the key is absent from the context.
  - A provider that does not acknowledge the signer fails boot and is closed.
  - An unresolved reference degrades, naming it.
  - CONTROL: `bearer` gets no signer.
- **Borrow:** `connector-credential-source.test.ts` covers the 422.
- **Providers:** `rest-provider.test.ts` and `openapi-provider.test.ts` cover every attempt signed (a retry included), the acknowledgement, a verification failure rejecting, the static CONTROL without acknowledgement, and static plus signer refused.
- **End to end:** `connector-rest-plugin.test.ts` runs a real host with the rest provider. Two calls carry ACS3 `Authorization` headers with different nonces and signatures, and the key appears in no call and no descriptor.
- **Suites:**
  - spec integration plus pins: 13 files, 211 passed.
  - service-automation signing, materialization and credential source: 93 passed.
  - connector-rest: 32 passed.
  - connector-openapi: 75 passed.
- `pnpm --filter <pkg> typecheck` is green for spec, service-automation, connector-rest and connector-openapi.
- Ablations: the host's acknowledgement check removed ⇒ the two boot-refusal pins red; the signature cached across attempts ⇒ the per-attempt pin red; the rest provider not passing the signer ⇒ 4 pins red, the end-to-end one among them. With the code as pushed, all green.
- Every family `dispatch-gates --commands` derives (115) ran and exited 0, reconciled with `--ran`: 115 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, after a dependency-closure build and the pinned teardown fixture fetch. `pnpm lint` exits 0.

Skills-docs: `grep -rlnE "credentialRef|app-credential|api-key" skills` hits `skills/objectstack-automation/{SKILL.md,references/integration-recipes.md,evals/integrations-declared.json}`, which list the instance auth kinds. The `signed` text rides #28226 (the skills follow-up for the ADR-0143 kinds), because a `skills/**` edit would make this slice Tier H. `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx` carries it here.

## Human Minimum

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic. (The signing wrap extends the existing `connectorFetchOptions` transport helper, which already lives in spec beside `resilientFetch`. It holds no crypto; signers live in `service-automation`.)
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `pnpm lint` passes.
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request (slice 1 of 3 of #26710).
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed.
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [x] 8. Title, body and comments are in English (the 维护者速读 block is the lane's maintainer summary).
